Welcome to Lionheart School
Attendance Notification for Parents/Carers
Dear Parents and Carers,
We hope you and your family have had an enjoyable summer break.
We are writing to inform you of a change to the school day which comes into effect from the start of this academic year.
New School Day Timings
An email containing this information was scheduled to be sent via Parent Mail before the summer holiday. Unfortunately, due to a technical issue with the system, the message was not successfully delivered. We sincerely apologise for this oversight and any inconvenience or confusion this may have caused.
Please ensure that your child arrives at school in good time each day to be ready for registration and the start of lessons at 8:30am.
On Fridays, although students finish earlier at 1:10pm, a lunch will still be provided at 12:40pm before students leave for the weekend. Please take this into account when making transport or collection arrangements.
For those on bespoke timetables, arrangements will continue as discussed, please contact the school if you have any questions regarding this.
The revised timetable has been implemented to support students’ learning, wellbeing and the effective delivery of the curriculum across the school week.
If you have any questions regarding the change to the school day or require any support with transport or collection arrangements, please do not hesitate to contact the school office.
Thank you for your understanding and continued support. We look forward to welcoming students back and working together for a successful academic year.
We are a Local Authority Maintained Pupil Referral Unit on the Isle of Wight. Lionheart School is a nurturing and supportive environment designed to provide Safe, Supportive, Nurturing provision for every student who walks through our doors.
Admissions to The Lionheart School are not made through direct application by parents or carers. Instead, all placements are made through referral by the Isle of Wight Local Authority in accordance with specific criteria.
Monday to Thursday: 8:30am – 3:00pm
8:30am – 1:10pm

SEND
Golden Thread
This is supported by our Trauma-Informed approach, delivered by all staff.
Please click below to read more.

SEND
Teaching & Learning
What is phased learning?
Phased learning allows students to progress at their own pace by breaking down the curriculum into manageable chunks, enabling students to master each phase before moving on to the next.
This approach to teaching and learning helps to reduce anxiety and build a solid foundation of knowledge, ensuring that students are fully prepared for future challenges.
What are task cards?
Task cards provide clear, step-by-step instructions for specific tasks or activities, helping students stay focused and organized.
Task cards can be tailored to individual learning needs and are particularly useful for breaking down complex tasks into manageable steps.
This approach not only enhances understanding and retention but also promotes independence and self-confidence in students. This provides structured opportunities for students to regulate.
This approach allows Lionheart school to make a positive impact on young lives, helping students overcome barriers, and guiding them towards a brighter future.

CURRICULUM
English
This includes developing critical thinking, appreciating cultural diversity whilst building a strong foundation for future learning and participation in society.

CURRICULUM
Maths
We focus on building core skills and knowledge at key stage 3 before working towards a range of qualifications across the four areas of number, algebra, geometry and statistics.
All students work towards an AQA entry level certificate by the end of year 10. Students on a dual registered placement also work towards completing this while they are with us as it provides evidence that the key scaffolding to be successful at GCSE are in place.
Students then work towards AQA GCSE entry at foundation (1-5) or higher (4-9) tier depending on ability and confidence.
Whilst we do not routinely work towards functional skills (Pearson level 1/2), it is appropriate for some students to build confidence so can be taken in discussion with teaching staff.
For further information on our maths curriculum or schemes of work please contact jane.griffiths@lionheart.iow.sch.uk

CURRICULUM
Relationships, sex & health education
The curriculum area of RSHE equips children and young people with the information, skills and values they need to have safe, respectful and enjoyable relationships, and empowers them to take responsibility for their sexual health and wellbeing.
They also develop an understanding of the wider world they live in and how history, culture and religious beliefs have worked together to form our unique society.

CURRICULUM
Our Remote Learning Offer
At The Lionheart School, we are committed to ensuring that every student has access to high-quality education, whether learning takes place in school or remotely. To support this, we work in partnership with Academy21, a leading online learning provider.
Academy21 delivers live, interactive lessons taught by qualified teachers across a wide range of subjects. This platform allows our students to:
Our remote learning offer ensures continuity of education for students who cannot attend school in person, while maintaining the same high standards of teaching and learning. By combining our school’s support with Academy21’s expertise, we provide a flexible, inclusive, and effective learning experience.
For more information about our remote learning provision or to discuss individual needs, please contact the school office.
DfE Accredited Online Alternative Provision | Academy21

CURRICULUM
Science
Students study key ideas in chemistry, physics, and biology through practical and theory work, helping students to build their confidence, skills, and knowledge.
At KS3, students study the AQA Activate scheme of work from Kerboodle, which offers appropriate preparation for the GCSE course. They also complete a variety of projects, which have included 3D design, building marble rollercoasters, and measuring the pollution levels of water from sites across the Island.
We offer GCSE’s in AQA combined science (Trilogy), as well as the separate sciences at KS4. This enables students can move on to careers in Science, Technology, Engineering and Maths. We also offer AQA Entry level science. Lionheart students also learn how to be healthy, and how to think critically about areas of science which are evolving in modern life.
More information about the curriculum can be found here: Science | Subjects | AQA

ABOUT US
OFSTED Report
Ofsted (the Office for Standards in Education, Children’s Services and Skills) is the national body that inspects and regulates services providing education, training, and care for children and young people. This includes schools, colleges, early years settings, and organisations that support vulnerable learners. Its role is to make sure these services are safe, high‑quality, and helping children achieve the best possible outcomes. [gov.uk], [gov.uk]
Ofsted publishes inspection reports that highlight a school’s strengths and areas for development. These reports help parents understand how well a school is performing and support schools to continue improving. In recent reforms, Ofsted has introduced clearer report cards and a new 5‑point grading system designed to give families more accessible, meaningful information.

Parents & Students
Information for parents & students

Parents & Students
Assessments, Exams & Qualifications
At Lionheart School, we know that our students may have small to significant gaps in their knowledge and skills. On arrival, students undertake baseline assessments in a calm and relaxed atmosphere during their induction. We use the outcomes to to design our provision for each student. During the induction , students may be tested for specific learning needs which we can support them with during their time here.
Throughout key stage 3 and 4, all students are assessed informally and formally. In each lesson, students will be aware of the expectations and objective(s they are working towards. We ensure that students have ownership over their learning and learn to identify which steps they should take next.
Key Stage 3 Students are assessed in each subject area based on their skills on a termly basis. Teacher judgements are made to inform next steps for planning to ensure students make good or better progress. We run a flexible roll on/ off programme designed to address individual learning needs and transition students towards the end of Year 9 into GCSE, Functional skills or Edexcel awards as appropriate
Key Stage 4 At the end of Year 10, students take mock exams. We use these as well as work evidence to decide which accreditation students should work towards. Year 11 mock exams take place in January.
All students in year 11 take the Entry level as a stepping stone to GCSE.
GCSE levels awarded- 1-9 (Foundation 1-5 or higher tier paper level 4-9 for Maths)
BTEC- Food, Art, PE, Vocational studies Level 1 Pass/ Merit/ Distinction Level 2 Pass/ Merit/ Distinction
Functional Skills (English/ Maths) -This course prepares students for further study at college. It is appropriate for students who lack the confidence to sit the GCSE paper when they are in year 11.
Entry Level– For students working below level 2 GCSE or who have significant gaps in their knowledge and skills, this is undertaken with staff to ensure that they have accreditation in each subject.

Parents & Students
Attendance
At Lionheart School we aim to support all of our young people to ensure they access a broad and balanced curriculum that provides them with the best possible learning opportunities and experiences.
Excellent levels of attendance are critical to ensure positive outcomes for all students on academic, personal, social and emotional levels.
It is very important to be punctual and to arrive at the school on time. A positive start to the day is conducive to a successful day. When students arrive between 9.00am and 9.30am, they will be marked as present. Arrival between 9.30am and 10.00am they will be marked as late and after 10.00am will result in a mark of unauthorised absence for the morning.
Evidence needs to be provided to the Lionheart School Admin Staff so that these incidences can be authorised. Where possible we respectfully request that appointments are made outside school hours.
Lionheart School is part of the Isle of Wight local authority and therefore operates the same approach to this as Island mainstream settings. We respectfully request that no holidays are requested or taken during term time. A leave of absence can only be granted by the Head teacher in exceptional circumstances.
The application must be made in advance, in writing to the Head Teacher with reasons why the request satisfies ‘exceptional circumstances’. When holidays are taken that do not fall into this category, the absences will be recorded as unauthorised.
Healthier Together – should your child go to school today? Click the link to view/download NHS advice (opens in the new window).

Parents & Students
School Organisation
We currently have 5 tutor groups at our Newport site and 6 at our Cowes site. In addition we have an online learning offer and also tutors who may visit students who are unable to come in to school.
This provision provides tailored support for students at risk of exclusion, helping them re-engage and thrive in their education.
3a and 3c are mostly year 7-9 students
4a is mostly year 10
4c and 4d are mostly year 11.
There are occasions when students will be taught in mixed year groups.
This is our section 19 provision for students who because of exclusion, illness or other reasons, would not receive suitable education without such provision.
LHA is mostly year 7 and 8 students
LHB is mostly year 9 students
LHC is mostly year 10
A small number of students attend the main school in the afternoon, depending on their needs.

SEND
Trauma Informed Practice at Lionheart School
Vision statement
Our aim is to create a culture of understanding, support and growth that promotes the holistic well-being of all students, linking to our values of Respect, Strength and Achieve, helping students build a strong foundation for the future.
Rationale – why adopt a trauma-informed approach?
We recognise that not all young people will have experienced trauma; however by adopting trauma informed principles and practice this will benefit all students through the focus on building positive relationships and connections.
There is growing research that indicates Positive Childhood Experiences (PCE’s) can reduce or mitigate the impact of ACE’s, with it highlighted that this is possible through the provision of safe and nurturing relationships and environments. These can be provided across the school, home and wider community.
With this in mind we support our student’s wellbeing and readiness for learning through a holistic approach to education where the individual needs of the child/young person are central to our practice and individual children/young people are supported to recognise and meet their holistic needs, to promote their safety, wellbeing and engagement in all areas of their lives including their education.
Ethos of the Trauma Informed Approach at Lionheart School
To provide the children and young people that have experienced trauma and who attend Lionheart School with access to an environment and support that recognises the impact of their trauma on their wellbeing, development and ability to access and engage in their education.
To provide an environment and support that is safe and sensitive to the needs of the individual students that access it to prevent further or re-traumatisation.
To support the school system of ‘People, Place and Purpose’ by providing a safe environment, with a relationships first approach, promoting a sense of belonging, identity and self-efficacy.
The staff team are knowledgeable and confident with understanding the importance of attachment and the impact of ACE’s for engaging children and young people in their learning. We seek to identify barriers to wellbeing and learning and support the children and young people to address these, empowering them and promoting feelings of safety, choice and control over their lives.
Model
Alongside this, as part of our planned future professional development, we will utilise Dr Hughes’ Dyadic Developmental Psychotherapy (DDP) model, implementing elements of the DDP model to enable us to provide support for children who experience challenges with feeling safe and secure as a result of traumatic experiences.
DDP seeks to support children/young people to establish, repair and maintain relationships.
